draft.title: Horizontal and vertical lines
card: Every point on a horizontal line has the same y value, so its equation is \(y = c\). The line \(y = 3\) passes through \((-2, 3)\) and \((5, 3)\).
Every point on a vertical line has the same x value, so its equation is \(x = c\). The line \(x = 2\) passes through \((2, -2)\) and \((2, 4)\).
A horizontal line has gradient 0. A vertical line has no gradient. The equation \(y = c\) names the height of the line, and \(x = c\) names where it crosses the x-axis.
Parallel lines have the same gradient. All horizontal lines are parallel to each other, and so are all vertical lines.

1.alt: The horizontal line \(y = 3\) passing through the points \((-2, 3)\) and \((5, 3)\), and the vertical line \(x = 2\) passing through the points \((2, -2)\) and \((2, 4)\).

draft.remember: \(y = c\) is a flat line at height \(c\). \(x = c\) is an upright line through \(x = c\).

a.q: Which line passes through the points \((4, -1)\) and \((4, 6)\)?
a.why: Both points have an x value of 4, so the line is vertical with equation \(x = 4\). The option \(y = 4\) mixes up the two axes: it is a horizontal line through height 4.
a.clue: Which coordinate is the same in both points?

b.q: Mia's garden fence is the line \(y = -2\). A second fence is parallel to it and passes through \((3, 5)\). What is the equation of the second fence?
b.why: The line \(y = -2\) is horizontal, so a parallel line is also horizontal. Every point on it has the same y value, which is 5 here, so it is \(y = 5\). The option \(x = 3\) is a vertical line, which is not parallel to a horizontal one.
b.clue: A horizontal line has the same y value everywhere.
